reason: This passage (Exodus 12) describes the final plague and the Exodus from Egypt. The text documents God's instructions through Moses, the striking of the firstborn, Pharaoh's command to release the Israelites, and the obedient departure of the Hebrew people. The narrative explicitly states that the Israelites 'did according to the word of Moses' (וּבְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל עָשׂוּ כִּדְבַר מֹשֶׁה) and followed instructions without complaint. While Pharaoh experiences distress at the plague, there is no recorded instance of the Hebrew people themselves voicing criticism against Moses, Aaron, or Yahweh in this fragment. The passage emphasizes obedience and divine favor rather than complaint.
